newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower on slack business, hedges.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower on slack business, hedges.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed lower on a lack of tangible export business and on hedge selling, traders said.
"Shay (Shay Grain) sold it right out of the box and took it down to the day's lows and it didn't recover," a trader said.
Shay sold roughly one million bushels of March wheat amid thin volume, they said.
Cash merchandisers early Wednesday said there were signs farmers were selling a little more wheat. "The farmer seems to be turning a bit more (wheat) loose," a Kansas dealer said.
Wheat futures were underpinned by talk this week India and Egypt were in the market for optional-origin wheat.
Dry weather in the U.S. Great Plains was underpinning new crop July but there were some forecasts for rain early next week in portions of the Plains wheat growing region.

Technicials cited support in the March in the $4.15 to $4.16 per bushel area. Spreaders said the March/July traded at 60 to 61 cents, premium March. Refco Inc did 200,000 bushels of the March/May, the traders said.
KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed unchanged to three cents per bushel lower, with March down 2-1/2 at $4.16.
